facts.text: Goshen started in 1874 as College Grove, renamed 1876, and grew into a bustling hub with stores, a flour mill, a blacksmith shop, and a schoolhouse‑church.
The Tisdale Store‑Goshen Post Office at 119 Turtle Road earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Places, honoring its role in the town’s history.
Archival photos of early Goshen, including Vol Walker with Moses Dutton, are housed in the Shiloh Museum of Ozark History.
Mill Branch Park offers 163 acres of Ozark forest and trails, plus Twin Bridges where the White River meets Richland Creek.
Nestled in the Ozark Mountains, Goshen embodies the spirit of community and the beauty of nature.
Goshen’s community building hosts weddings, meetings, and gatherings for residents.
